unitChecks.sourceWitness: 姚泓
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Heading identifies Yao Hong.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 姚泓，字元子，興之長子也。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Yuanzi is Xing’s eldest son and Yuanzi his courtesy name.

unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong’s filial/fraternal virtues, mildness, poor health and want of governing ability explain Xing’s hesitation.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 久之，乃立為太子。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: After a long interval Xing made Hong crown prince.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 興每征伐巡遊，常留總後事。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: On tours or campaigns Xing left Hong to oversee affairs behind him.

unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong loved learning, discussion and poetry.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 尚書王尚、黃門郎段章、尚書郎富允文以儒術侍講，胡義周、夏侯稚以文章遊集。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Three titled men taught Confucian learning; two others joined Hong for literature.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 時尚書王敏、右丞郭播以刑政過寬，議欲峻制，泓曰：「人情挫辱，則壯厲之心生；
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Two named officers urge stricter measures; Hong says humiliation breeds fierceness.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 政教煩苛，則苟免之行立。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Onerous government produces conduct aimed merely at escaping punishment.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 上之化下，如風靡草。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Influence from above bends those below as wind bends grass.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 君等參贊朝化，弘昭政軌，不務仁恕之道，惟欲嚴法酷刑，豈是安上馭下之理乎！」
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong rebukes the officials for insisting on cruel penalties and questions how that can secure their ruler and govern his subjects.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 敏等遂止。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Min and the others desist.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 泓受經于博士淳于岐。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong studied the classics under the erudite Chunyu Qi.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 岐病，泓親詣省疾，拜於床下。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong personally visited the sick teacher and bowed below his bed.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 自是公侯見師傅皆拜焉。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Dukes and marquises thereafter bowed to their tutors.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 興之如平涼也，馮翊人劉厥聚眾數千，據萬年以叛。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: During Xing’s visit to Pingliang, Liu Jue mustered thousands and seized Wannian in revolt.

unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong dispatched Peng with Eastern Palace guards; Jue was beheaded and his followers pardoned.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 諸將咸勸泓曰：「殿下神算電發，蕩平醜逆，宜露布表言，廣其首級，以慰遠近之情。」
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: The generals praise Hong’s rapid strategy and suggest a public victory report with a magnified tally of enemy heads.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 泓曰：「主上委吾後事，使式遏寇逆。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: The sovereign entrusted the rear to Hong to suppress rebels.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 吾綏禦失和，以長奸寇，方當引咎責躬，歸罪行間，安敢過自矜誕，以重罪責乎！」
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong admits his mishandling encouraged rebellion and rejects self-glorification that would compound his guilt.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 其右僕射韋華聞而謂河南太守慕容築曰：「皇太子實有恭惠之德，社稷之福也。」
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Wei Hua tells the Henan governor that Hong’s respectful kindness is a blessing for the state.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 其弟弼有奪嫡之謀，泓恩撫如初，未嘗見於色。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong’s younger brother Bi plotted for the heirship, and Hong kept his manner unchanged.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Although Shao supported Bi, Hong treated Shao sincerely and deferentially.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 及僭立，任紹以兵權，紹亦感而歸誠，卒守其忠烈。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: On assuming the throne Hong gave Shao command; moved by this trust, Shao proved loyal to the end.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 其明識寬裕，皆此類也。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: The episode exemplifies Hong’s judgment and magnanimity.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 興既死，秘不發喪。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Xing’s death was initially kept secret.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 南陽公姚愔及大將軍尹元等謀為亂，泓皆誅之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong executed the duke, the grand general and their fellow conspirators.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 命其齊公姚恢殺安定太守呂超，恢久乃誅之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong ordered Hui to kill Lü Chao; Hui obeyed after a long delay.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 泓疑恢有陰謀，恢自是懷貳，陰聚兵甲焉。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong suspected Hui; Hui developed divided loyalties and secretly gathered arms.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 泓發喪，以義熙十二年僭即帝位，大赦殊死已下，改元永和，廬於諮議堂。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong announced mourning, assumed the throne in Yixi 12, pardoned even capital offenders, changed the era and occupied mourning quarters.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 既葬，乃親庶政，內外百僚增位一等，令文武各盡直言，政有不便於時，事有光益宗廟者，極言勿有所諱。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: After burial Hong governed personally, promoted all officials and solicited candid advice about policy and benefit to the dynasty.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 初，興徙李閏羌三千家于安定，尋徙新支。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Xing moved three thousand Qiang households of Lirun, first to Anding and soon to Xinzhi.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 至是，羌酋党容率所部叛還，遣撫軍姚贊討之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Chief Dang Rong led his following in revolt to return home; Hong sent Zan against him.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 容降，徙其豪右數百戶于長安，余遣還李閏。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: After Rong surrendered, several hundred powerful households moved to Chang’an; the rest went back to Lirun.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 北地太守毛雍據趙氏塢以叛于泓，姚紹討擒之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Mao Yong rebelled from the Zhao stockade; Shao attacked and captured him.

unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Unaware of Yong’s defeat, Xuan sent his officers from Lirun to protect Chang’an.

unitChecks.checkedPropositions: After the force set out, the scheming Wei Zong warned Xuan of the new ruler’s unestablished authority and the danger of Bobo.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 殿下居維城之任，宜深慮之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Wei reminds Xuan that he is a bulwark of the ruling house.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 邢望地形險固，總三方之要，若能據之，虛心撫禦，非但克固維城，亦霸王之業也。」
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Xingwang commands three approaches; from there Xuan could protect the dynasty or found a dominion himself.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 宣乃率戶三萬八千，棄李閏，南保邢望。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Xuan abandoned Lirun, taking 38,000 households south to hold Xingwang.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 宣既南移，諸羌據李閏以叛，紹進討破之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: The Qiang rose at Lirun; Shao advanced and defeated them.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 宣詣紹歸罪，紹怒殺之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Xuan acknowledged guilt before Shao, who killed him in anger.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 初，宣在邢望，泓遣姚佛生諭宣，佛生遂贊成宣計。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: While Xuan was at Xingwang, Hong sent Fosheng to speak to him; Fosheng supported Xuan’s plan.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 紹數其罪，又戮之。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Shao recited Fosheng’s crimes and executed him too.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 泓下書，士卒死王事，贈以爵位，永復其家。
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: The decree gave posthumous titles to soldiers and perpetual exemption to their families.

unitChecks.sourceWitness: 將封宮臣十六人五等子男，姚贊諫曰：「東宮文武，自當有守忠之誠，未有赫然之效，何受封之多乎？」
unitChecks.checkedPropositions: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons; Zan objected that ordinary loyalty without conspicuous merit did not warrant such extensive grants.

repairs.before: He was dutiful, gentle, and kind, but had no talent for governing a realm, and he was often ill—so Yao Xing long hesitated before naming him heir.
repairs.after: He was dutiful to his parents, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild. But he lacked the ability to govern and was often ill, so Yao Xing hesitated over making him heir.
repairs.sourceWitness: 孝友寬和，而無經世之用，又多疾病，興將以為嗣而疑焉。
repairs.sourceReason: 孝友 includes devotion to siblings as well as filial piety.

repairs.before: He was filial, friendly, generous, and mild, yet lacked the ability to order the age, and moreover often fell ill; Xing was about to make him heir yet hesitated.
repairs.after: He was filial, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild, yet lacked the ability to govern the realm and was often ill. Xing intended to make him heir but hesitated.
repairs.sourceWitness: 孝友寬和，而無經世之用，又多疾病，興將以為嗣而疑焉。
repairs.sourceReason: 友 in 孝友 denotes affection toward siblings.

repairs.before: Wang Shang, Duan Zhang, and Fu Yunwen tutored him in the classics; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi kept him company over belles-lettres.
repairs.after: Wang Shang, a master of writing, Duan Zhang, a gentleman of the Yellow Gates, and Fu Yunwen, a gentleman of the Department of State Affairs, tutored him in the classics. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him for literary gatherings.
repairs.sourceWitness: 尚書王尚、黃門郎段章、尚書郎富允文以儒術侍講，胡義周、夏侯稚以文章遊集。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore the distinct offices of all three Confucian tutors.

repairs.before: Director Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and Director Gentleman Fu Yunwen attended lectures with Confucian learning; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi gathered in literary companionship.
repairs.after: Master of Writing Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs Fu Yunwen attended him as lecturers on Confucian learning. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him in literary gatherings.
repairs.sourceWitness: 尚書王尚、黃門郎段章、尚書郎富允文以儒術侍講，胡義周、夏侯稚以文章遊集。
repairs.sourceReason: 侍講 describes lecturing to Hong, not attending lectures as pupils; 尚書郎 is a departmental gentleman.

repairs.before: Director Wang Min and aide Guo Bo thought the laws too soft and pressed for crackdowns. Yao Hong replied: "Humiliate people and you breed defiance.
repairs.after: Wang Min, a master of writing, and Guo Bo, the right assistant director, thought the administration of punishments too lenient and proposed stricter regulations. Yao Hong replied, “Humiliate people and you breed defiance.
repairs.sourceWitness: 時尚書王敏、右丞郭播以刑政過寬，議欲峻制，泓曰：「人情挫辱，則壯厲之心生；
repairs.sourceReason: 右丞 specifies Guo’s office and 以刑政過寬 covers punishments and governance.

repairs.before: You help run the court—widen the path of mercy, not the jailer's whip; harshness is no way to steady ruler and people."
repairs.after: You gentlemen help guide the court and make its principles of government known. If you neglect humanity and clemency and seek only strict laws and cruel punishments, how can you keep the ruler secure and govern his subjects?”
repairs.sourceWitness: 君等參贊朝化，弘昭政軌，不務仁恕之道，惟欲嚴法酷刑，豈是安上馭下之理乎！」
repairs.sourceReason: The officials’ responsibility for exemplifying government policy and Hong’s rhetorical question about ruling above and below have been compressed away.

repairs.before: After that, every prince who met a tutor bowed as he had done.
repairs.after: After that, dukes and marquises all bowed when they met their tutors.
repairs.sourceWitness: 自是公侯見師傅皆拜焉。
repairs.sourceReason: 公侯 identifies dukes and marquises.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang with palace guards from the heir's residence; Liu Jue was executed and the rest pardoned.
repairs.after: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang, the General Who Guards the Army, to lead the Eastern Palace guards against Liu Jue. Jue was beheaded and the remaining rebels pardoned.
repairs.sourceWitness: 泓遣鎮軍彭白狼率東宮禁兵討之，斬厥，赦其餘黨。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore Peng’s military title and his commission to attack Jue.

repairs.before: His generals said: "Your victory was swift—publish a victory notice and show the heads to steady the realm."
repairs.after: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness devised your plans with lightning speed and swept away the vile rebels. You should issue an open dispatch reporting the victory and claiming a greater number of enemy heads, to reassure people far and near.”
repairs.sourceWitness: 諸將咸勸泓曰：「殿下神算電發，蕩平醜逆，宜露布表言，廣其首級，以慰遠近之情。」
repairs.sourceReason: 廣其首級 concerns the number of heads claimed in the report. Only Jue had been beheaded in the preceding unit. The generals also praise Hong’s swift planning.

repairs.before: The generals all urged Hong, saying, "Your Highness's divine calculations strike like lightning; you have swept away the vile rebels—it is fitting to issue a public bulletin reporting it, broadly display their heads, to comfort feeling far and near."
repairs.after: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness devised your plans with lightning speed and swept away the vile rebels. You should issue an open dispatch reporting the victory and claiming a greater number of enemy heads, to reassure people far and near.”
repairs.sourceWitness: 諸將咸勸泓曰：「殿下神算電發，蕩平醜逆，宜露布表言，廣其首級，以慰遠近之情。」
repairs.sourceReason: 廣其首級 concerns the number of heads claimed in the report. Only Jue had been beheaded in the preceding unit. The generals also praise Hong’s swift planning.

repairs.before: I mishandled the pacification and fed rebellion—I should blame myself, not strut and deepen my fault."
repairs.after: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”
repairs.sourceWitness: 吾綏禦失和，以長奸寇，方當引咎責躬，歸罪行間，安敢過自矜誕，以重罪責乎！」
repairs.sourceReason: The sentence connects failures of pacification and defense to the rise of rebellion and adds 歸罪行間 after Hong takes personal responsibility. Preserve the military setting without shifting the blame onto his subordinates.

repairs.before: I failed in pacification and control, thereby growing traitorous bandits; I ought to take blame on myself and assign guilt among the ranks—how dare I overmuch boast and swagger, thereby adding to the burden of fault!"
repairs.after: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”
repairs.sourceWitness: 吾綏禦失和，以長奸寇，方當引咎責躬，歸罪行間，安敢過自矜誕，以重罪責乎！」
repairs.sourceReason: The sentence connects failures of pacification and defense to the rise of rebellion and adds 歸罪行間 after Hong takes personal responsibility. Preserve the military setting without shifting the blame onto his subordinates.

repairs.before: Wei Hua told Murong Zhu: "The crown prince's humility is the dynasty's luck."
repairs.after: Hearing of this, Wei Hua, the right vice-director, told Murong Zhu, governor of Henan, “The crown prince truly is respectful and kind. That is a blessing for the state.”
repairs.sourceWitness: 其右僕射韋華聞而謂河南太守慕容築曰：「皇太子實有恭惠之德，社稷之福也。」
repairs.sourceReason: Both offices, Hua hearing the incident, and 惠 as kindness in addition to respectful humility are explicit.

repairs.before: His brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.
repairs.after: His younger brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.
repairs.sourceWitness: 其弟弼有奪嫡之謀，泓恩撫如初，未嘗見於色。
repairs.sourceReason: 弟 specifies a younger brother.

repairs.before: Yao Shao backed Yao Bi, but Yao Hong still trusted him as kin and showed no distrust.
repairs.after: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted and honored Shao wholeheartedly and bore him no suspicion on that account.
repairs.sourceWitness: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。
repairs.sourceReason: 宗事 entails deference or honoring Shao; 嫌 means Hong harbored no suspicion against him on this account.

repairs.before: Yao Shao often acted as wings for Bi; Hong also gave him whole-hearted clan duty and did not take it as suspicion.
repairs.after: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted and honored Shao wholeheartedly and bore him no suspicion on that account.
repairs.sourceWitness: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。
repairs.sourceReason: 宗事 entails deference or honoring Shao; 嫌 means Hong harbored no suspicion against him on this account.

repairs.before: Once Yao Hong took the throne he gave Yao Shao real command; Shao repaid him with loyalty unto death.
repairs.after: When Yao Hong claimed the imperial throne, he entrusted Yao Shao with military command. Moved by this, Shao pledged himself to Hong and remained loyal to the end.
repairs.sourceWitness: 及僭立，任紹以兵權，紹亦感而歸誠，卒守其忠烈。
repairs.sourceReason: 僭 conveys the narrator’s view of Hong’s imperial claim, and 感 gives Shao’s response to Hong’s trust.

repairs.before: Yao Yin, Yin Yuan, and their fellow plotters were put to death.
repairs.after: Yao Yin, Duke of Nanyang, Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion. Yao Hong put them all to death.
repairs.sourceWitness: 南陽公姚愔及大將軍尹元等謀為亂，泓皆誅之。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore both offices, the plot to rebel and Hong as the executor.

repairs.before: Yao Hong announced the death, and in the twelfth year of Yixi claimed the throne, declared a general amnesty short of capital crimes, adopted the era Yonghe, and mourned in a hut beside the council hall.
repairs.after: Yao Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he claimed the imperial throne, issued a general pardon extending even to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and took up quarters in a mourning hut at the council hall.
repairs.sourceWitness: 泓發喪，以義熙十二年僭即帝位，大赦殊死已下，改元永和，廬於諮議堂。
repairs.sourceReason: 殊死已下 includes prisoners sentenced to death and those with lesser sentences. Both fields reverse that scope.

repairs.before: Hong issued mourning; in the twelfth year of Yixi he presumptuously assumed the imperial seat, greatly pardoned all short of capital crime, changed the era to Yonghe, and lodged in a mourning hut at the consultation hall.
repairs.after: Yao Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he claimed the imperial throne, issued a general pardon extending even to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and took up quarters in a mourning hut at the council hall.
repairs.sourceWitness: 泓發喪，以義熙十二年僭即帝位，大赦殊死已下，改元永和，廬於諮議堂。
repairs.sourceReason: 殊死已下 includes prisoners sentenced to death and those with lesser sentences. Both fields reverse that scope.

repairs.before: After the funeral he took the reins himself, promoted every official a grade, and invited blunt counsel on what helped or hurt the state.
repairs.after: After the burial Hong took charge of government himself and promoted every official at court and in the provinces by one rank. He ordered civil and military officers alike to speak freely about policies unsuited to the times and measures that would bring honor and benefit to the dynasty, holding nothing back.
repairs.sourceWitness: 既葬，乃親庶政，內外百僚增位一等，令文武各盡直言，政有不便於時，事有光益宗廟者，極言勿有所諱。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore civil and military officials, the policy question, benefit to the ancestral dynasty and injunction to speak without reserve.

repairs.before: Their chief Dang Rong then bolted for home; Yao Hong sent Yao Zan against him.
repairs.after: The Qiang chief Dang Rong then led his followers in revolt and set out for home. Yao Hong sent Pacifying General Yao Zan to attack him.
repairs.sourceWitness: 至是，羌酋党容率所部叛還，遣撫軍姚贊討之。
repairs.sourceReason: The chief leads his following in revolt, and Yao Zan bears the Pacifying Army title.

repairs.before: Dang Rong yielded; Yao Hong moved the head families to Chang'an and let the rest go home to Li-run.
repairs.after: Dang Rong surrendered. Yao Hong moved several hundred of the leading households to Chang’an and sent the rest back to Lirun.
repairs.sourceWitness: 容降，徙其豪右數百戶于長安，余遣還李閏。
repairs.sourceReason: 數百戶 gives a specific approximate count.

repairs.before: Mao Yong of Beidi seized the Zhao stockade in revolt; Yao Shao captured him.
repairs.after: Mao Yong, governor of Beidi, occupied the Zhao clan’s stockade in revolt against Yao Hong. Yao Shao attacked and captured him.
repairs.sourceWitness: 北地太守毛雍據趙氏塢以叛于泓，姚紹討擒之。
repairs.sourceReason: 太守 makes Mao governor of Beidi, and he revolted against Hong.

repairs.before: Adviser Wei Zong, a troublemaker, told Yao Xuan: "The new ruler lacks prestige; Helian Bobo is too strong—the capital's troubles are not over.
repairs.after: After the troops had set out, Yao Xuan’s adviser Wei Zong, a deceitful flatterer who delighted in disorder, urged him, “The ruler has only just taken the throne, and his authority is not yet established. Helian Bobo is powerful, and his incursions are sure to cause great harm. Our court’s troubles cannot yet be put to rest.
repairs.sourceWitness: 眾既發，宣參軍韋宗奸諂好亂，說宣曰：「主上初立，威化末著，勃勃強盛，侵害必深，本朝之難未可弭也。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore the troops’ departure, Zong’s deceit and flattery, the predicted invasive harm and the threat to the court.

repairs.before: You hold the western shield—think hard.
repairs.after: Your Highness has the duty of protecting the ruling house. You should consider this carefully.
repairs.sourceWitness: 殿下居維城之任，宜深慮之。
repairs.sourceReason: 維城 depicts the prince’s duty as a bulwark of the state, without a western direction.

repairs.before: Xingwang is a natural fortress commanding three approaches—seize it in earnest and you secure the west and maybe build a power base."
repairs.after: Xingwang is naturally defensible and commands the approaches from three directions. If you occupy it and govern the people there with an open mind, you can secure your position as a bulwark of the dynasty and even lay the foundations of a hegemon’s or a king’s rule.”
repairs.sourceWitness: 邢望地形險固，總三方之要，若能據之，虛心撫禦，非但克固維城，亦霸王之業也。」
repairs.sourceReason: Recover willing and open-minded governance, the dynastic bulwark and the prospect of hegemonic or royal power.

repairs.before: Yao Xuan marched thirty-eight thousand households south from Li-run to fortify Xingwang.
repairs.after: Yao Xuan abandoned Lirun and led thirty-eight thousand households south to hold Xingwang.
repairs.sourceWitness: 宣乃率戶三萬八千，棄李閏，南保邢望。
repairs.sourceReason: 棄李閏 is abandonment of the garrison; 保 is holding the refuge at Xingwang.

repairs.before: When Yao Xuan left, the Qiang seized Li-run; Yao Shao smashed them.
repairs.after: Once Yao Xuan had moved south, the Qiang groups occupied Lirun in revolt. Yao Shao advanced against them and defeated them.
repairs.sourceWitness: 宣既南移，諸羌據李閏以叛，紹進討破之。
repairs.sourceReason: 以叛 is an explicit revolt.

repairs.before: Yao Xuan surrendered to Yao Shao, who killed him in fury.
repairs.after: Yao Xuan went to Yao Shao to acknowledge his guilt. Shao killed him in anger.
repairs.sourceWitness: 宣詣紹歸罪，紹怒殺之。
repairs.sourceReason: 歸罪 identifies Xuan’s acknowledgment of fault.

repairs.before: Earlier Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to recall Yao Xuan; Fosheng instead backed the defection.
repairs.after: Earlier, when Yao Xuan was at Xingwang, Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to reason with him. Fosheng ended up supporting Xuan’s plan.
repairs.sourceWitness: 初，宣在邢望，泓遣姚佛生諭宣，佛生遂贊成宣計。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore the location and avoid supplying a specific recall order or calling Xuan’s plan a defection.

repairs.before: He decreed pensions and perpetual exemptions for families of soldiers who died in royal service.
repairs.after: Yao Hong decreed that soldiers who died in royal service should receive posthumous titles and their families should enjoy perpetual exemption from levies.
repairs.sourceWitness: 泓下書，士卒死王事，贈以爵位，永復其家。
repairs.sourceReason: 贈以爵位 is the posthumous award of titles, not a pension for surviving relatives.

repairs.before: Yao Zan objected to raising sixteen household officers to noble rank: "The heir's staff owes loyalty by duty—they have done nothing spectacular yet."
repairs.after: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons. Yao Zan objected, “Surely the crown prince’s civil and military officers owe him loyalty as a matter of duty. They have shown no conspicuous merit. Why grant them so many fiefs?”
repairs.sourceWitness: 將封宮臣十六人五等子男，姚贊諫曰：「東宮文武，自當有守忠之誠，未有赫然之效，何受封之多乎？」
repairs.sourceReason: Restore Hong’s intention, the two noble ranks, the civil and military staff, and Zan’s question about the extensive grants.

repairs.before: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as fifth-rank barons and viscounts; Yao Zan remonstrated, saying, "Eastern-palace civil and military naturally ought to have the loyalty of guarding unto death—they have not yet had blazing manifest merit; how can they receive so many enfeoffments?"
repairs.after: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as viscounts and barons in the five grades of nobility. Yao Zan remonstrated, “The Eastern Palace’s civil and military officers naturally owe it faithful loyalty. They have yet to show conspicuous merit. Why should they receive so many grants of fiefs?”
repairs.sourceWitness: 將封宮臣十六人五等子男，姚贊諫曰：「東宮文武，自當有守忠之誠，未有赫然之效，何受封之多乎？」
repairs.sourceReason: 五等 is the five-grade system, not an ordinal shared by the fourth and fifth grades; 守忠 does not specify death.
